text:
Chris Jones to host election night event in Little Rock on November 3
Chris Jones will host an election night event in Little Rock as polls close on November 3. The event will include a press area for credentialed media and comes as Jones leads in a closely watched congressional race.
Chris Jones, the Democratic nominee for Arkansas’s 2nd Congressional District, will hold an election night event with supporters at the Hall in Little Rock on November 3. The event is scheduled to begin at 7:30 p.m. Central Time, coinciding with the closing of the polls. Doors will open at 7:00 p.m.
According to the announcement, there will be a designated press space at the event for credentialed media. All members of the press, including reporters, producers, photographers, and camera operators, are required to obtain a credential lanyard in person at the Chris Jones for Congress Headquarters, located at 921 W. Markham St., Little Rock, on Monday, November 2, between 12 p.m. and 6 p.m. Government-issued photo identification and outlet credentials are required for pickup. The campaign advises that credentials will not be issued at the event, and any members of the press unable to pick up credentials during the designated hours should contact the campaign before 6 p.m. on Monday.
Chris Jones is described as a rocket scientist, combat veteran spouse, minister, and father, running for Congress in Arkansas's Second District. The campaign states that Jones is a son of Pine Bluff, rooted in faith, family, service, and a commitment to telling the truth and fighting for a future that works for all.
Jones is seeking to unseat Republican incumbent and banker French Hill in what is described as one of the most-watched congressional races of 2026. Jones currently leads by four points, according to the most recent independent poll. Arkansas’s 2nd Congressional District is included on the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee’s Red to Blue list, according to Chris Jones for Congress.
The election night event is open to supporters and credentialed media, with preparations in place to accommodate press coverage as results come in.
